messages.subject: Bug in log_mix?
parts:
I'm preparing to analyze some circular-domain data so I was playing with simulating a mixture model of a uniform & von Mises and happened upon a combination of parameters that yielded decidedly strange looking samples. To eliminate the von Mises as a distribution known to have numeric issues, I tried a normal and got the same result. Here's the normal+uniform mixture model:

data {
  real<lower=0,upper=1> prob ;
  real<lower=0> sigma ;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=-1,upper=1> y ;
}
model {
  target += log_mix(
    prob
    , normal_lpdf( y | 0 , sigma )
    , uniform_lpdf( y | -1 , 1 )
  ) ;
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bug in log_mix?
parts:
To answer your direct question, you can see if log_mix is doing the
right thing by comparing

target += log_mix(p, lp1, lp2);

with

target += log_sum_exp(log(p) + lp1, log1m(p) + lp2);

They should produce the same result.

But you're going to have a problem because you restrict y to (-1, 1)
but don't constraint the normal_lpdf. This is usually OK under
two conditions: (1) no Stan parameters are involved as parameters (violated
by your model), and (2) you don't use them in mixtures (also violated
by your model). The solution's the same here --- you need to do the
explicit truncation with normal_lpdf(), using instead:

normal_lpdf(y | 0, sigma) - (log(normal_cdf(1, 0, sigma) - normal_cdf(-1, 0, sigma))

- Bob
